source.snippet: AI companies started with very cheap subscriptions and it's been hardly 1 year and costs has increased 10-50x in a lot of cases. A lot of companies are still using Coding agents as they don't want to miss out on AI. Corporates are spending up to $500 per month per employee and local AI models are becoming good. So companies can just spend 1000 USD more on a beefy 128GB machine...

problem_statement: Companies are paying $300–$500/month per developer for AI coding subscriptions with no tooling to track ROI, optimize seat allocation, or evaluate when switching to local models would be cheaper — resulting in uncontrolled and unjustified AI tooling spend.
target_segment: CTOs, engineering VPs, and IT procurement managers at mid-market software companies (20–500 employees) with multiple AI tool subscriptions.
notes: Single HN post with low score (3), but the $500/month/employee figure is a concrete and credible budget signal. The commenter frames this as a decision companies are actively making. Adjacent to the SaaS spend management category (Zylo, Torii) but specific to AI tooling. A solo operator could build a lightweight AI spend dashboard or a 'should you go local?' calculator. Buyer intent is moderate — no explicit 'I'd pay for this' but the cost pain is quantified.
